svg.title: MR-1 wiring schematic: Octopus Pro v1.1, four CL57T V4.1 drives
svg.desc: One-page overview of power, command, alarm, home, probe, operator, spindle and coolant wiring. Planning drawing; dashed HOLD items are not designed or qualified.
svg.text: BTT Octopus Pro v1.1 (STM32F429, grblHAL) · 4 × CL57T V4.1 closed loop · stock spindle servo
PLANNING DRAWING. NOT APPROVAL TO ENERGIZE OR MOVE. Dashed = HOLD (not designed or not qualified). Printed terminal names on the real parts win over this page.
always on · feeds Octopus, PS-ALM, relays
24 V only · 28 V abs max · never 36 V
PF3 contact is part of the HOLD stop design.
Healthy = low. Fully verified bare NC contacts may go direct to GND.
(5-pin header silked BLTouch: PB7 + GND only; PC5 PROBE port unused)
E-STOP + SAFETY RELAY (needs a reviewed design)
Dual-channel E-stop and interlocks. On stop it must:
· open the motion contactor (36 V off, Z-drop plan)
· remove spindle-servo energy (contactor / STO, not SON)
· cut coolant pump and air-solenoid supply
One fused star branch per drive (no daisy chain). Never 36 V to the Octopus.
PE: bond backplate, frame, DIN rail and each drive chassis directly.
All GPIO 3.3 V. No field 5 V or 24 V on any pin.
· A1 A2 B1 B2 motor outputs, all 8
relay contacts 11–14 in series · 100 nF on each input
PS-ALM +Vo → F-ALM → every relay A1 (+23 V).
Input from 24 V PSU via its own fuse. Relay 12/22 empty.
low-side outputs: verify rail jumpers first
STOCK SPINDLE SERVO (DB44, community map: meter first)
16 = SON via dry contact to 24 V I/O 0 V
FLOOD PUMP (supply in hardwired stop chain)
MIST / AIR SOLENOID (supply in hardwired stop chain)
Three separate returns: Octopus GND · CTRL_0V (DRIVER0 GND) · ALM 0V (PS-ALM −Vo).
Never join them because they are all called GND.
ALL FOUR CL57T — SET WITH POWER OFF
Socket STEP 7 · DIR 8 · GND 9 · VCC_IO 10 (DRIVER0 only) are schematic
contact IDs, not a pin count. Find pin 1 on the real board first.
PB1 is the only drive-fault stop. PG12–PG15 only report which axis.
Never energize a drive without its motor and encoder connected.
1. P4 reversed: kills the drive (P4 is polarized)
2. 36 V into Octopus MAIN POWER: kills the board
3. S3 on 5V with 24 V signals: destroys the input
4. Raw ALM, stock 5 V or 24 V on any Octopus GPIO
5. Hot-plugging P3 motor or P4 power
6. Driver jumpers or DIAG links left on the sockets
